resources.string: Please enable the accessibility service manually
Start the screen-off mode service first
This app does not collect, record, or upload any of your information.\n
Tap to start the screen-off mode service

Screen-off mode requires ADB or root permission.

To activate with ADB: enable USB debugging on your phone, connect it to a computer, and run this command in a terminal: 
adb shell %s

On Android 6.0 and later, you can also activate with Shizuku (it provides the same permission as ADB activation).
ADB command copied to clipboard: \nadb shell %s

You can open this help screen at any time by tapping the Screen-off mode title on the main screen.


During screen-off mode, all apps continue running as they do when the screen is on. You do not need to worry that the system will sleep after a period of inactivity. As long as global control is enabled, the system will not sleep automatically unless you press the power button.


When Raise to wake is enabled, the app monitors device orientation changes after entering screen-off mode. This slightly increases power usage, but the effect is negligible.


Note: Most devices disable touch after entering screen-off mode, so double-tap to wake works on only a few devices (including known Samsung S Pen tablets, iQOO 9, and Redmi Note 1 LTE).


Some devices disable hardware keys after entering screen-off mode, so volume-key wake does not work on them (including some Huawei HarmonyOS and OriginOS devices). If you have such a device, contact us to explore detecting volume keys with getevent.


Some LCD devices keep the backlight on after entering screen-off mode. Like disabled keys and touch, this is determined by the system and cannot be changed. You can lower the screen brightness before entering screen-off mode to minimize the backlight.
